title: QPS cliff and degraded quantization fallback audit - customer escalation
content:
Summary:

This doc captures the investigation and mitigation for a customer-reported incident where a burst of non-uniform traffic caused a sharp QPS cliff and SLO misses for multiple hosted endpoints between 2026-03-09 10:23Z and 2026-03-09 11:12Z. Customer observed 95th pct latency regressions from ~120ms to >1.2s and sustained error rates from retries and timeouts.

High-level timeline (UTC):
- 2026-03-09 10:20 — Canary alerts: a single customer’s route shows latency creeping up.
- 2026-03-09 10:23 — Automated SLO alert fired (route: /v1/generate, model: rwd-ggml-7b-q8a).pager paged on-call.
- 2026-03-09 10:28 — On-call triage: brief rollback to previous kernel selection policy attempted (no effect).
- 2026-03-09 10:35 — Eng team captures flamegraphs and nvprof samples from a replication node.
- 2026-03-09 10:42 — Escalation call with customer; they provided request traces and prompt length distribution showing high variance.
- 2026-03-09 10:58 — Hotfix candidate identified: force-disabling dynamic quantization fallback heuristics (git PR #1324).
- 2026-03-09 11:04 — Hotfix applied to 4 nodes in the affected pool; latency returns to baseline for those nodes.
- 2026-03-09 11:12 — Rollout to full pool completed; SLOs green.

Symptoms observed:
- Abrupt per-node CPU usage spikes on host-side inference process concurrent with increased memory bandwidth utilization (measured with sar/pidstat and perf counters).
- GPU utilization remained moderate for affected nodes (20–45%), but end-to-end latency rose due to long tail CPU-side stalls (~600–900ms extra).
- KV-cache hit-rate stayed similar. Batching behavior changed: batch sizes shrank unexpectedly for affected endpoints (more small batches), increasing overhead.
- Kernel selection logs showed repeated attempts to use a fused int8 transformer kernel but falling back to a slower emulation path on the CPU when batch size and sequence length combination hit a corner case.

Root cause hypothesis (final):
A recent change to the quantization kernel selection heuristics (merged 2026-02-28) introduced an optimistic fast-path preference for a new int8 fused GPU kernel. The selection logic allowed the fast-path for cases with quantized weights but did not fully account for the interaction with non-uniform request footprints (high variance in seq_len and per-request token counts). Under these input distributions, the fused kernel sometimes failed late in the GPU launch (driver-level kernel compile/ld failure or internal assert) and the runtime triggered a synchronous fallback that executed a CPU-based emulation routine. That fallback path was not async-aware and blocked the inference thread, causing CPU stalls, increased memory copies, and a reduction in effective QPS.

Why it manifested as a QPS cliff:
- The fallback path serialized work on the inference thread (no offload), increasing per-request CPU time from ~10ms to ~600ms in worst cases.
- The scheduler's continuous-batching heuristics reacted to longer latencies by shrinking batch windows, further degrading throughput (positive feedback loop).
- A small portion of requests hitting the corner case caused head-of-line blocking for coalesced batch workers on several nodes simultaneously, producing the observed cliff.

Evidence collected (selected):
- Kernel selection logs (snippet):
  [2026-03-09T10:30:12Z] DEBUG select_kernel: candidate=quant_fused_int8_gpu; validation=ok; launch_status=ENQUEUE_FAILED -> fallback_to_cpu_emulation
  [2026-03-09T10:30:12Z] WARN kernel_fallback: emulation_ms=612; stack=serve::request::process->runtime::fallback_handler
- Perf counters: DRAM throughput spike from 18GB/s -> 75GB/s during fallback windows (node-id a3f4).
- Flamegraph top functions during incident: runtime::fallback_handler, memcpy_async, scheduler::wait_for_batch, runtime::token_emit. CPU-bound profile dominated by memcpy and emulation loops.
- Microbenchmarks: synthetic harness reproduced emulation fallback when running mixed seq_len distribution (seq_len samples: 8, 12, 512, 64). Pure uniform loads did not trigger the bug.
- Customer traces: mid-request kernel logs showing `LAUNCH_ERROR` inside driver logs concurrent with fallback entries in application logs.

Immediate remediation taken:
1) Hotfix PR #1324 — changed kernel selection to perform a defensive post-launch check and avoid synchronous CPU emulation path. Instead: if GPU launch fails, mark kernel as blacklisted for this model/variant for N minutes and fall back to a pre-validated slower GPU-compatible path or serialized GPU-safe kernel.
   - Rollout to affected pool at 11:04 recovered most nodes quickly.
2) Rate-limited canary before full rollout to observe side-effects. Metrics: 95th latency returned to ~130ms on canary nodes within 90s.
3) Short-term customer communication: emailed a technical summary + mitigation steps and offered a follow-up postmortem and credits for SLA miss.

Validation & benchmarking performed post-hotfix:
- Replayed customer traffic through a staging pool with and without hotfix.
- Microbenchmark harness: 10k requests with mixed sequence-length distribution; failure-to-fallback rate dropped from ~0.8% to 0.01%.
- End-to-end latency distributions: p50 unchanged, p95 improved from 1.02s -> 134ms, p99 improved from 1.6s -> 210ms on staging.
- Stress test for 24 hours with realistic variance: no new synchronous CPU fallback events observed.

Longer-term fixes and action items:
- engineering: add unit/integration tests to kernel selection that include mixed sequence-length distributions and force-driver failure injection (JIRA-ENG-2148). Owner: Liam. ETA: 2026-04-06.
- runtime: implement async fallback path that does not block inference thread; push heavy emulation to worker pool, and keep lightweight path on critical thread. Owner: Ethan. ETA: 2026-05-01.
- observability: expose a kernel-fallback metric (per model-variant, per-node) and add alert if fallback rate > 0.1% for 5m. Owner: Rosa. ETA: 2026-03-21.
- product: add note to model catalog describing known quantization caveats and fallback behavior; surface recommended request-size limits for older quantized kernels. Owner: Maya. ETA: 2026-03-30.

Customer-facing summary (for CS):
We traced the regression to a recent optimization that selected a faster quantized GPU kernel in some edge cases. When the GPU kernel failed to launch for a small subset of mixed-length requests, our runtime synchronously executed a fallback emulation routine on CPU which blocked the inference thread and caused a cascade of latency and throughput degradation. We deployed a fix that changes the fallback to avoid synchronous CPU blocking and blacklists problematic kernels for short windows. We validated this against the customer workload and saw restoration of SLOs.

Draft postmortem notes to be expanded:
- Incident window, impact (customer ids, number of requests affected, duration) — TODO (requires CS metrics).
- Root cause: kernel-selection + sync CPU fallback path under mixed seq_len distribution.
- Corrective actions: hotfix, observability, async fallback, test coverage.
- Prevent recurrence: safety gates on kernel selection merges, include driver failure injection in CI.

Appendix - commands & artifacts used during debug:
- Collected flamegraphs: ./tools/profiler/capture_flamegraph.sh --pid 8421 --duration 60 --out /tmp/flame-8421.svg
- Perf counters snippet: sudo perf stat -e L1-dcache-loads,LLC-loads,mem_uops_retired.all_loads -p 8421 -I 1000
- Microbenchmark harness: python tools/bench/mixed_seq_bench.py --model rwd-ggml-7b-q8a --requests 10000 --seq-dist "[8,12,64,512]"
- Hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1324 (apply -> rollback steps included in PR comments)
- Driver logs: /var/log/nvidia-driver/driver.2026-03-09.log (attached to incident ticket)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a working audit; logs and some customer metrics are redacted from this doc. Please validate mitigation wording before we publish a customer-facing postmortem.
- If you reproduce the CPU fallback locally, capture both GPU driver errors and the application kernel selection traces — both were required to pinpoint the race/validation gap.
